results.claim: Post-threat behaviour: render first aid when safe, and follow instructions given by law enforcement and first responders.
results.citedSource: CISA Active Shooter Preparedness Action Guide (June 2025), https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/2025-06/Active-Shooter-Preparedness-Action-Guide_508_20250611.pdf
results.evidence: URL resolves. Document text carries 'Render first aid when safe to do so.' and 'When help arrives, follow instructions given by law enforcement and first responders.' It also carries 'If unable to safely evacuate, hide in a secure area where access or entryways can be locked', which supports the pre-all-clear keyed action.
results.advisory: The second citation in the same meta.source, the 2019 CISA hospitals action guide at the legacy /publications/19_0515_cisa_action-guide-hospitals-and-healthcare.pdf path, did not surface in search. CISA has since republished that resource as 'Physical Security Considerations for Healthcare and Public Health Facilities'. The legacy URL may be stale. This citation is pre-existing, not introduced by this iteration, and every keyed proposition in the row is independently carried by the verified 2025 guide, so this is advisory rather than blocking. Worth a link-freshness pass later.

results.claim: The two ADA-permitted questions, no certification/documentation requirement, no demonstration requirement, handler responsible for the animal's care, removal permitted only when the animal is out of control and the handler does not take effective action, with services still offered.
results.citedSource: DOJ, Frequently Asked Questions about Service Animals and the ADA, https://www.ada.gov/resources/service-animals-faqs/
results.evidence: FAQ Q7 states that where it is not obvious the dog is a service animal, staff may ask only whether the dog is a service animal required because of a disability and what work or task it has been trained to perform, and that staff may not request documentation, require a demonstration, or inquire about the disability. The out-of-control/no-effective-action removal rule and the hospital access rule (service animals allowed wherever patients and the public may go) were also confirmed.
results.advisory: meta.source cites Q7, Q9, Q14-Q15, Q17, Q25, Q28. Q7 is confirmed as the two-questions answer. The remaining Q-number mapping was not individually confirmed; every substantive proposition was confirmed to be in that FAQ. Citation precision, not factual accuracy.
results.constructNote: q02_r2 is correctly framed as a counterfactual ('If the dog's task were not apparent'). This matters: the stem states the seizure-alert task, so in the scenario as written the two questions would not in fact be permitted. The conditional framing keeps the row accurate rather than contradicting the stem.

results.claim: Disclosure of separately maintained psychotherapy notes requires valid written authorization; the originator's own treatment use and the covered entity's supervised mental-health training programme are listed exceptions; treatment by a clinician who did not create the notes is not.
results.evidence: Regulation text confirmed verbatim: a covered entity must obtain an authorization for any use or disclosure of psychotherapy notes except, at (a)(2)(i)(A), 'Use by the originator of the psychotherapy notes for treatment', and at (a)(2)(i)(B), 'Use or disclosure by the covered entity for its own training programs in which students, trainees, or practitioners in mental health learn under supervision...'. Non-originator treatment disclosure appears in no exception, so authorization is required. Both distractors map exactly onto the two cited listed exceptions and the key maps onto the residual case.
results.advisory: FAQ 558 was not separately opened. The governing regulation is the primary source and was verified verbatim, which is the stronger check; the FAQ is corroborative only.

results.claim: CDC recommends not wearing artificial fingernails/extenders during direct contact with high-risk patients (ICU, OR), and keeping natural nail tips under 1/4 inch; CDC does not impose a universal ban on intact nail polish.
results.citedSource: CDC Clinical Safety: Hand Hygiene for Healthcare Workers, https://www.cdc.gov/clean-hands/hcp/clinical-safety/index.html; CDC Guideline for Hand Hygiene in Health-Care Settings, Recommendations 6.A-6.B
results.evidence: Recommendation 6.A confirmed: 'Do not wear artificial fingernails or extenders when having direct contact with patients at high risk (e.g., those in intensive-care units or operating rooms) (IA).' Recommendation 6.B confirmed: 'Keep natural nail tips less than 1/4-inch long (II).' The CDC clean-hands clinical safety page carries the same artificial-nail restriction. No universal intact-polish prohibition appears in the cited guidance, so q17_s08 is correctly keyed as unsupported.
results.thresholdNote: The 1/4-inch figure is a threshold. It is sourced, not authored from model memory, and it now appears only in post-answer rationale, not in scored text.

section107Status.rationale: Section 10.7 requires Stage 2 to recompute every current publishable payload hash and require equality with the latest governing AFFIRM, and section 11.1 makes publication-freeze.json Stage 3's sole publication authority. This seat cannot recompute any hash. Writing the freeze now would populate Stage 3's sole authority with thirteen digests transcribed from the producer's own report; Stage 3's pre-flight would then compare the current draft against numbers derived from that same draft by that same seat, so the check would agree by construction and detect nothing. That is precisely the self-certification the work order forecloses at section 0.5, and it would convert a capability gap into a false attestation carried on an immutable artifact. The nine AFFIRMs are content dispositions and are not weakened by this; the freeze is a distinct artifact with a precondition this seat cannot meet.
section107Status.unblockPath: Owner recomputes, from the current raw draft using the repository's own stableJson and sha256 under the campaign convention: the nine revised payload hashes, the four AFFIRM payload hashes, and the raw draft's file-byte SHA-256. If those thirteen plus one agree with the producer-reported values recorded here, the anti-self-report purpose of section 9.2 item 1 is discharged and this seat can write the section 10.7 freeze on owner-computed values in the same Stage 2 seat. If any disagree, the disagreement itself is the finding and the affected rows return to section 10.
